content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To remember the five great lakes, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Design a mnemonic poster for the bedroom wall (1 hour)
Step 2. Research the surface area of Lake Superior (20 minutes)
Step 3. Recite the names to a family member (5 minutes)
Step 4. Label a blank map of the Great Lakes region (15 minutes)
Step 5. Find a documentary about the glacial formation of the lakes (90 minutes)
Step 6. Look up the depth of Lake Baikal for comparison (10 minutes)
Step 7. Take a self-timed quiz on lake locations (10 minutes)
Step 8. Memorize the "HOMES" acronym (5 minutes)
Step 9. Pinpoint Lake Michigan on a digital globe (5 minutes)
Step 10. List the major cities on the shores of Lake Erie (15 minutes)
Step 11. Create flashcards for the volume of each lake (30 minutes)
Step 12. Read a Wikipedia overview of the Great Lakes system (20 minutes)
Step 13. Write a short paragraph about Lake Ontario (15 minutes)
Step 14. Watch a short clip about the Edmund Fitzgerald (10 minutes)
Step 15. Explain the outflow of the St. Lawrence River (15 minutes)
Step 16. Compare the water temperatures of the five lakes (20 minutes)
Step 17. Search for photos of each lake's shoreline (25 minutes)
Step 18. Identify the states that border Lake Huron (10 minutes)
Step 19. Sketch the unique shape of Lake Michigan (10 minutes)
Step 20. List the invasive species found in the lakes (20 minutes)
Step 21. Learn about the Niagara Falls connection (30 minutes)
Step 22. Color-code the lakes on a physical map (15 minutes)
Step 23. Note which lake is entirely within the US (5 minutes)
Step 24. Find the elevation levels of each lake (20 minutes)
Step 25. Listen to a podcast about Great Lakes shipwrecks (45 minutes)
Step 26. Rank the lakes from largest to smallest (10 minutes)
Step 27. Identify the primary fish species in Lake Michigan (15 minutes)
Step 28. Research the environmental threats to the lakes (40 minutes)
Step 29. Download a geography study app (5 minutes)
Step 30. Buy a set of colored markers (15 minutes)
Step 31. Locate the Straits of Mackinac (10 minutes)
Step 32. Review the spelling of "Sault Ste. Marie" (5 minutes)
Step 33. Write a poem using the lake names (30 minutes)
Step 34. Record yourself naming the lakes from memory (2 minutes)
Step 35. Post a picture of your study notes online (5 minutes)
Step 36. Print out high-resolution satellite images (10 minutes)
Step 37. Read a travel blog about a road trip around the lakes (35 minutes)
Step 38. Check a weather map for the Great Lakes region (5 minutes)
Step 39. Learn about the "lake effect" snow phenomenon (20 minutes)
Step 40. Summarize the economic importance of the lakes (25 minutes)
Step 41. Gather all necessary study materials (10 minutes)
Step 42. Trace the flow of water from Superior to the Atlantic (30 minutes)
Step 43. Study the history of trade on the lakes (1 hour)
Step 44. Create a digital folder for lake facts (5 minutes)
Step 45. Tell a friend a fun fact about Lake Huron (2 minutes)
Step 46. Look up the meaning of the word "Huron" (5 minutes)
Step 47. Give a 2-minute presentation to a pet or plant (2 minutes)
Step 48. Note the average freezing dates for each lake (15 minutes)
Step 49. Clear a workspace on the desk (10 minutes)
Step 50. Find a map showing the drainage basin (15 minutes)
Step 51. Bookmark a reliable educational website (5 minutes)
Step 52. Set a reminder to review the facts tomorrow (1 minute)
Step 53. Watch a video on the formation of the Niagara Escarpment (15 minutes)
Step 54. Compare the shoreline lengths (15 minutes)
Step 55. Locate the Welland Canal on a map (10 minutes)
Step 56. Buy a notebook for geography studies (15 minutes)
Step 57. Scan a textbook chapter on North American geography (20 minutes)
Step 58. Write the acronym "HOMES" on a sticky note (1 minute)
Step 59. Find a topographical map of the region (15 minutes)
Step 60. Read about the indigenous names for the lakes (30 minutes)
Step 61. Recite the lakes in order of depth (5 minutes)
Step 62. Draw a diagram of the lake lock systems (25 minutes)
Step 63. Research the salt mines under the lakes (20 minutes)
Step 64. Look up the definition of an "endorheic basin" (5 minutes)
Step 65. Visit a library or online archive (1 hour)
Step 66. Verify the coordinates of the northernmost point (10 minutes)
Step 67. Learn the lyrics to a song about the lakes (20 minutes)
Step 68. Practice drawing the lakes from memory (15 minutes)
Step 69. Look up the water clarity of Lake Superior (10 minutes)
Step 70. Final mental rehearsal of all five names (1 minute)
